answer.evidence: The tall standing sign is mostly a face-on panel. Rows 9-28 are the blue board with white lettering, and rows 29-31 are a dark base. The header at rows 0-8 is wider (16 against 14) and has only a 1-2 row lighter blue top band at rows 1-2 with no ellipse or contents. Rows 3-5 are a face-on white label, and rows 6-8 are dark blue shadow. This is only a rim-like strip, not a real top surface. The main body shows no horizontal surface, so it is a front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a vertical blue sign with a dark navy outline that leans blue (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, like all references), so the outline is a tinted material tone rather than a sticker-black line. It has 8 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so no large flat fills. The body shows a light edge highlight, a mid blue and a dark side, with white sign glyphs and a lighter top cap, about 4 shading steps against roughly 5 on the references. Texture is limited to the glyphs and a few edge pixels, with no grain or speckle. At 2x it looks a little simpler and flatter than kiosk-a and vending-a, which carry more panel detail, small items and shading clusters. It is acceptable next to bus-shelter-a, but slightly thinner than the richer references, and the call is borderline. When in doubt, fail.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a navy standing sign with a lighter blue rim highlight, a pale label panel with glyph text, and a rounded top cap. It has about 4 shading steps on the blue body against about 5 on the references, which is slightly shallower, and it lacks the grain of the vending machine.
